AISettingIn.description: Send what changes: the source, the QueryLab model, or both.
AISettingIn.title: AISettingIn

ImportCreatedOut.description: Returned once, when the import is created: where to PUT the file.
ImportCreatedOut.title: ImportCreatedOut

LLMModelsOut.description: The models a user may pick, per provider; the first of each list is the default.
LLMModelsOut.title: LLMModelsOut

PendingOut.description: What a person is asked to approve, so the screen needs no step parsing.
PendingOut.title: PendingOut

get.description:
What is left before a limit: asks on the shared default key today, unfinished
runs against the cap, whether you saved your own key, and open live streams.
The limits are yours, not per workspace; `workspace` only checks that it is
one you may use (404 otherwise) and is echoed back. Read only.

Your runs, newest first unless `ordering` says otherwise (`created_at` or
`latency_ms`, `-` for descending). Filter by `status` (repeat it for several),
`q` (text in the question) and `created_after` / `created_before`. `meta.count`
is the number of runs that match.

post.description:
Start a run on the demo, or on one of your own workspaces (`workspace`).
The agent plans and proposes SQL, then waits for approval; follow it on
`/runs/{id}/events`. One run counts as one spend of the shared default key.
Runs on your own workspace are kept out of eval data.

get.description: A run and its steps. Poll this when the live stream is not available.

post.description: Run the SQL the agent proposed. Only while the run waits for approval.
End a paused run without running anything.

Run your own SQL instead. It goes through the same guard; a refusal is a 400
and the run stays paused.

get.description:
Server-sent events: `step` for each step, then one `status` event when the
run pauses for approval or ends. Event ids are step indexes; reconnect with
`Last-Event-ID` to continue. Over the open-stream limit it answers 429
`agent_stream_limit`: poll `GET /runs/{id}` instead.

put.description:
Rate your own finished run: `up` or `down`, with an optional short note.
One vote per run; sending it again changes it. 409 `run_not_finished` while
the run is still going. It only helps choose runs worth reviewing.

get.description:
The stored trace in order. No model call and no query on the demo database:
it is read from the steps alone.

The rows of a succeeded run, up to the row cap. Rows are not stored: this
runs the run's stored SQL again, through the guard, on the read-only
connection. It never takes SQL from the request, so the numbers can differ
from the first run if the data changed. 409 `run_not_succeeded` otherwise.

post.description:
Answer a question about the demo database, or about one of your own
workspaces (`workspace`): the SQL that ran, the result table and a confidence
score. The SQL is checked before it runs and runs on the read-only connection
of that workspace only.

get.description:
Every dependency the backend needs. Not wrapped in the envelope, so
uptime checks can read `status` directly; 503 when anything fails.

The signed-in user's saved keys: provider, last four characters, model.
The key itself is never returned.
The models allowed per provider (from settings).

put.description: Check the key with the provider and save it encrypted.
Make this key the one your asks use (the other one stops being active).
Switch the model of a saved key; the key is not sent again.
Choose QueryLab's AI or your own, and the model used on QueryLab's key.

get.description:
The signed-in user, or 401. The frontend's route guards use this.

Also sets the csrftoken cookie (signed in or not): the app calls this
first on every load, so its first POST already has a token to send.

Every table of the demo schema, or of your workspace (`workspace`), with
columns, keys, comments and row estimates. Send `If-None-Match` with the last
`ETag` to get a 304 when nothing changed.

One table, same shape as in the full schema. An unknown name is a 404
`table_not_found` that says nothing else about the schema.

A read-only page of one table's rows, in primary-key order when it has one.
The table must exist in the schema (an unknown name is a 404 `table_not_found`);
the SQL is built here from catalog names only, never from the request, and runs on
the same reader connection as every other read. Page size is capped by
PAGINATION_MAX_LIMIT.

Staff only. Trace cases, newest source run first, with the model's draft (or
why it failed), the reasons the run was picked and a link to its trace. Filter by
`status` (repeat it) and `cluster`. `meta.count` is the match count.

post.description:
Staff only. Queue a drafting batch (at most TRACES_DRAFT_MAX_PER_BATCH cases,
one LLM call each, counted on your daily default-key allowance). Drafts show up
on `GET /cases` as `drafted`.

get.description:
Staff only. One case with a preview of its rows: the draft is guarded and run
on the reader now (the rows are shown, never stored).

post.description:
Staff only. Make a drafted case gold. Send `sql` (and `question`) to correct
them; either way the SQL is guarded and run again first. A draft that failed its
checks needs `sql` (422 `draft_unusable`). 409 `case_not_reviewable` unless the
case is `drafted`.
Staff only. The right answer is to decline: approved with no gold SQL.
Staff only. Keep a drafted case out of the eval set, with a reason.

get.description:
Staff only. The trace cases grouped by outcome, tables and SQL shape, then
merged when their questions overlap. Largest first, each with a label, a
representative and its case counts per status. Computed from the stored
`cluster_key`s (`build_trace_cases` and drafting refresh them).

Staff only. Two runs on the same target, case by case: the shared cases,
which flipped to wrong or to correct, the accuracy difference in percentage
points (on the shared cases) and the difference per cluster. 422
`eval_runs_not_comparable` when the targets differ.

Staff only. Eval runs, newest first, with accuracy, cost per question (null
when the model has no price in EVAL_MODEL_PRICES) and finish time. Filter by
`target`, `runner`, `model`, `prompt_version` and `status`.

Staff only. One run with its per-case results (question, gold SQL, predicted
SQL, outcome, reason, and a link to the source trace) and accuracy per cluster.
`meta.count` is the number of results; page through them with `limit`/`offset`.

Staff only. Runs on the shared demo that are allowed in evals (runs on a
user workspace never appear). Filter by `status`, `error_code`, `check`
(`checked` / `needs_look`), `key_source`, `revisions_min`, `edited`, `feedback` (`up`/`down`), `q` (text
in the question) and `created_after` / `created_before`. Order by
`created_at`, `latency_ms`, `revisions`, `llm_calls` or `row_count`, newest
first by default. `meta.count` is the number of matches.

Staff only. One run in full: every step (plan, tools, approval, execute
preview, reflect), the SQL the agent proposed first, the SQL finally approved
and `diff` when the person edited it. Result rows are not stored, so none are
shown beyond the stored preview. A workspace run is a 404.

The shared demo workspace first, then your own, with table counts and bytes
used. `meta.max_workspaces` is the cap.

post.description:
Create a private workspace: an empty schema only you and your agent can
reach. `workspace_limit_reached` when you already have the maximum.

delete.description: Always refused: the shared demo workspace cannot be deleted.

patch.description: Always refused: the shared demo workspace is read-only for everyone.

get.description:
What the caller may still do with workspaces: how many workspaces, how many
bytes (per workspace and together), and
the largest dump. Read only.

delete.description:
Drop the workspace's schema, tables and login roles for good. Your past
agent runs stay in your history and can still be replayed.

get.description:
One of your workspaces. Someone else's workspace is a 404, the same as a
missing one.
The workspace's last ten imports, newest first.

post.description:
Start a dump import. Send the file's name (`.sql` or `.sql.gz`) and exact
size in bytes; PUT the file to `upload_url` with that exact length, then call
`start`. Fails with `workspace_not_empty` at run time unless `replace` is set
or the workspace has no tables.

get.description: The status of one import; poll until `succeeded` or `failed`.

post.description:
Say the upload is done. Checks the file is in the bucket and within the
cap, then queues the job; poll `GET` for the result.

Run your own read-only SQL on your own workspace: `SELECT`, `WITH`,
`EXPLAIN`, `SHOW` or `VALUES`, one or several statements in one read-only
transaction. Anything that would change data or structure is refused with
`sql_invalid` before it runs, and the database role cannot write either.
A failing statement answers 422 `sql_failed` with the Postgres code and
message; one that runs too long is stopped (`query_timeout`). To change the
data, import a new dump.
